 Brewers use one of the most remarkable rallies in World Series history to take a big lead on Tampa
 Updated
 10:39 PM EDT, Mon October 26, 2026
 Oct 26, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Milwaukee Brewers catcher William Contreras (24) celebrates with outfielder Garrett Mitchell (5) after scoring against the Tampa Bay Rays during the fifth inning in game three of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images 
 Nathan Ray Seebeck/Imagn Images/Reuters 
 Ad Feedback 
 What we're watching here
 Milwaukee dominating: Game 3 of the 2026 World Series seemed like it was a near-must-win game for the Tampa Bay Rays. The Milwaukee Brewers entered the game with a 2-0 lead in the best-of-seven series
 Brewers are dominating: The Brewers used a couple of soft hits to strike first, but then used a huge, eight-run fifth inning rally – all with two outs – to take a commanding lead. It’s 10-0 in the eighth.
 World Series history: The Brewers’ fifth-inning rally set two new records in the Fall Classic. The seven consecutive two-out hits was a record, as was the eight-run burst the Brewers scored with two outs.
 Two wins away: The Brewers last appeared in the World Series in 1982 and have never won a championship. They appear on track to rewrite franchise history – unless Tampa has a miracle comeback in store. No team has ever come back from a 0-3 deficit in the World Series.

 Rays are making this too easy for Milwaukee
 By Hannah Keyser 
 The goal for the Brewers now is to get their most trusted, and oft-relied upon, relievers an extra day of rest by keeping them out of the game.
 The goal for the Rays should be to force Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy to dip into his circle of trust.
 The Rays are failing at that goal now, too, along with the “winning a baseball game” goal. Gasser is gone, but the Rays are still retired in order in the seventh.
 Score: Brewers 10, Rays 0

 Link Copied!
 Progress for the Rays - they retired Jackson Chourio
 By Kevin Dotson 
 Garrett Cleavinger came on to pitch the seventh inning for the Rays, and proceeded to sit the Brewers down in order.
 Even more impressively, Cleavinger managed to strike out Brewers’ lead-off man Jackson Chourio, who had been 4-for-4 in the game to that point.
 Barring a historic comeback, the Brewers are poised to push the Rays to the brink of elimination.
 It's been a tough night for Rays fans at The Trop pic.twitter.com/iIrBK5IfaH 
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 27, 2026 
 Score: Brewers 10, Rays 0

 Link Copied!
 Rays should try getting hits, it seems to work for the other guys
 By Hannah Keyser 
 Tampa Bay players watch from the dugout. 
 Chris O'Meara/AP 
 The Rays lead off the sixth with a walk from Victor Mesa, Jr.
 Then Nick Fortes grounds into a double play, Taylor Walls grounds out, and somehow Robert Gasser has still faced the minimum in this lopsided clinic being put on by the Brewers.
 Stunned faces in the Rays dugout. pic.twitter.com/rFddKDE673 
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 27, 2026 
 Gasser is first Brewers pitcher to get even a single out in the sixth inning this whole postseason, and he completes the frame easily.
 Score: Brewers 10, Rays 0

 Link Copied!
 It's death by 1,000 cuts for the Rays
 By Kevin Dotson 
 It has been a game to forget for Cam Booser and the Tampa Bay Rays. 
 Ashley Landis/AP 
 The Brewers started the 6th inning with 13 hits to the Rays’ one, and Milwaukee went looking for more.
 William Contreras and Brice Turang got back-to-back infield hits and the Brewers once again had ducks on the pond.
 Cole Sulser managed to escape the inning unscathed, but the Brewers are putting on a textbook example of their “small-ball” style that has confounded opponents all season.
 Remarkably, the Brewers have put up a 10-spot through six innings without the benefit of a home run.
 Score: Brewers 10, Rays 0

 Link Copied!
 Going down 10-0 didn't motivate the Rays offense
 By Hannah Keyser 
 It is highly unlikely that the Rays will come back in this game. And they definitely will not come back in this game if they continue to go down in order.
 Ironically, Tampa still has the three hardest-hit balls of the game – including Yandy Díaz’s 115.5 mph single, which is the hardest hit ball of the postseason.
 Yandy Díaz’s 115.5 mph leadoff single is the hardest-hit ball of this postseason thus far
He has each of the top two
— Sarah Langs (@SlangsOnSports) October 27, 2026 
 Baseball is weird sometimes!
 Brewers 10, Rays 0

 Brewers keep piling on
 By Kevin Dotson 
 Sal Frelick scores for Milwaukee during the fifth inning. 
 Jamie Squire/Getty Images 
 New pitcher, same result for the Brewers – and we’ve got history in the World Series.
 David Hamilton smacked a single into center field off Cole Sulser to score Sal Frelick.
 The @Brewers just keep on hitting!
It is now 9-0 Milwaukee in the 5th! pic.twitter.com/I429wpfopP 
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 27, 2026 
 Jackson Chourio, who is just 22, then came up and collected his second hit of the inning, a double to plate Hamilton from first base. Next, Jake Bauers mercifully hit a flyout to end the inning.
 JACKSON CHOURIO IS 4-FOR-4
HE HAS TWO HITS THIS INNING
IT'S 10-0 BREWERS 😱 pic.twitter.com/A39hkGwYGd 
— MLB (@MLB) October 27, 2026 
 But the damage was done – seven consecutive two-out hits from the Brewers to put this game out of reach, a World Series record.
 Milwaukee’s eight runs in the inning are two more than the Rays have scored so far in the entire series. It’s also a World Series record for most runs in an inning scored by a team with two outs.
 Score: Brewers 10, Rays 0

 Brewers have broken Game 3 wide open
 By Kevin Dotson 
 Milwaukee's Garrett Mitchell scores during the fifth inning. 
 Ashley Landis/AP 
 Rays third baseman Junior Caminero made a nice leaping catch to rob David Hamilton of a hit to start the fifth inning.
 It was a good thing, too, because Jackson Chourio came up next and collected his third hit of the game.
 Jake Bauers hit a flyout, then Christian Yelich worked Freddy Peralta for a walk, and the Brewers suddenly had a chance to break the game wide open.
 The Brewers’ postseason hero William Contreras was up next and hit a chopper to third base, but Yelich beat the throw from a spinning Caminero at second, setting up a bases loaded situation.
 That was the end of the line for Freddy Peralta, who was replaced by Cam Booser to face Brice Turang.
 Brice Turang makes it 4-0 @Brewers after Taylor Walls had a tough read on that ball in the 5th pic.twitter.com/jHTZYH9MTA 
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 27, 2026 
 Turang then smashed a ball right back through the box and off the glove of Taylor Walls. Chourio and Yelich scored as the ball trickled into center field.
 That started the hit parade.
 Garrett Mitchell adds another! pic.twitter.com/psQOzYk2OM 
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 27, 2026 
 The Brewers kept the pressure on with a single from Garrett Mitchell and a double from Cooper Pratt to plate three more runs and suddenly this game is out of hand.
 THE HIT PARADE CONTINUES FOR THE @BREWERS !
Cooper Pratt's two-run double makes it 7-0 Milwaukee! pic.twitter.com/7Dnajvhw4T 
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 27, 2026 
 Sal Frelick then hit a double into the left field corner to bring Pratt in with yet another run.
 Six two-out runs have crossed for the Brewers in the inning, and they’re still batting as the Rays make another pitching change.
 Score: Brewers 8, Rays 0

 Why baseball teams party so hard and so often in October
 By Don Riddell 
 The Milwaukee Brewers celebrate after winning the National League Championship Series earlier this month. 
 Ashley Landis/AP 
 At the end of this series, the final party will begin. It will be the last in a long line of them.
 Every major US sport has multi-round postseason schedules, but none of them party like MLB teams. Locker room celebrations in the NFL tend to be subdued until the Super Bowl, and since hockey players are famously superstitious, popping bottles early is practically verboten in the NHL; the Stanley Cup is all that really matters.
 Boston Red Sox clubhouse manager Tom McLaughlin has spent over 40 years with the Red Sox, and he says he’s lost track of how many celebrations he’s been involved in, but he counts them in the dozens. He told CNN Sports it was “pretty tame” when he started in the ‘80s, when the postseason was much shorter, but the back end of the season now can feel like one enormous bender for the most successful teams.
 Clinched a playoff spot? Party.
 Successfully navigate the wildcard round? Let’s get wild.
 Made it through the Divisional Round? Get another round in.
 Won the Championship Series? We’re going on a spree.
 By the time a baseball club wins the World Series , let’s just say that the celebration will not be their first rodeo. Everyone will have had plenty of practice.
 Read more here on why baseball teams party all the time, party all the time, party all the time in October.

 Rays continue to go quietly
 By Hannah Keyser 
 William Contreras had the most challenges among catchers in the regular season and he flexes that propensity again to help Robert Gasser complete another 1-2-3 inning.
 While we’re at it, the Brewers have been calling Contreras “Bill.” That’s all I’ve got to make this post interesting. Rays, help me out!
 Score: Brewers 2, Rays 0

 The Tropicana Field crowd comes to life as Peralta works a 1-2-3 inning
 By Kevin Dotson 
 A young Rays fan cheers for his team at Tropicana Field. 
 Ashley Landis/AP 
 Freddy Peralta performed a rare feat in the 4th inning – he retired the Brewers in order.
 Peralta struck out Garrett Mitchell and Cooper Pratt, which injected some much-needed life into the crowd in St. Pete.
 A groundout from Sal Frelick ended the inning in quick fashion, but the Rays need to find a way to break up the rhythm of Brewers’ starter Robert Gasser and do it quickly.
 Score: Brewers 2, Rays 0

 Robert Gasser is cruising through the Rays lineup
 By Hannah Keyser 
 Brewers starter Robert Gasser is off to a great start through three innings. 
 Elsa/Getty Images 
 Through three the Rays are making solid contact off Robert Gasser – two of the outs in that frame were over 100 mph off the bat – but he’s managed to face the minimum and given up just a single hit, back in the first.
 In a word: he’s cruising, with credit to the Brewers defense, which has been airtight so far tonight.
 Score: Brewers 2, Rays 0

 Brewers break through with a pair of runs
 By Kevin Dotson 
 Milwaukee's William Contreras connects on an RBI hit off Freddy Peralta. 
 Morry Gash/AP 
 Another inning, another rally for the Brewers.
 After a quick out, Jackson Chourio laced another single – his second of the game already – and Jake Bauers drew a walk, and Freddy Peralta was right back in the soup.
 This time, they cashed in as Christian Yelich hit his second bloop single of the game to bring Chourio in for the first run of the game.
 The @Brewers captain comes through in Game 3!
Christian Yelich drives in the first run of the game pic.twitter.com/OgfmNMfuNR 
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 27, 2026 
 On the very next pitch, William Contreras dropped a single into right field where Victor Mesa, Jr. struggled to field it cleanly, allowing Bauers to score.
 Contreras is caught between bases after the hit, but is still able to bring in another Brewers run pic.twitter.com/Mi5ctVry8g 
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 27, 2026 
 Peralta escaped the inning without any further damage, but the Rays once again find themselves in the unenviable position of playing catch-up against the Brewers.
 Score: Brewers 2, Rays 0

 The Rays go down on 5 pitches in the second
 By Hannah Keyser 
 Chandler Simpson keeps the game scoreless and… so do the Rays’ hitters. Tampa’s heart of the order goes down 1-2-3 on just five pitches.
 They got, you could say, gassed. (Robert Gasser is pitching.)

 The Rays' Chandler Simpson makes the catch of the series
 By Kevin Dotson 
 Tampa Bay's Chandler Simpson makes a leaping catch before crashing into the left-field wall in the second inning. 
 Jamie Squire/Getty Images 
 This Brewers offense is just relentless, and once again they got the leadoff man on – this time courtesy of a Freddy Peralta walk to Garrett Mitchell.
 But the Rays defense took Peralta off the hook in a big way.
 After a strikeout of Cooper Pratt, left fielder Chandler Simpson made about as good of a catch as you’ll ever see to rob Sal Frelick of extra bases and possibly save a run.
 WHAT A CATCH 😱 pic.twitter.com/C7K5a0Wyxe 
— MLB (@MLB) October 27, 2026 
 Then catcher Nick Fortes caught Mitchell stealing to end the inning and fire up the crowd in Tropicana Field.
 Score: Brewers 0, Rays 0 
 Read more 
 Link Copied!
 A baserunning mistake ends the Rays' first inning
 By Hannah Keyser 
 Tampa Bay's Chandler Simpson is tagged out by Brice Turang on a steal attempt in the first inning. 
 Chris O'Meara/AP 
 Chandler Simpson is fast. So fast that he can beat out a would-be double play to wind up on first.
 So fast that, once safely at first, you have to assume he’s a guarantee to attempt to steal second.
 So fast that, even if the pitcher knows he’ll be running, Simpson can still make it to second before the throw from the catcher.
 So fast, apparently, that he’ll actually go a little too far, and wind up tagged out after over-sliding the bag.
 Chandler Simpson came off the bag on his stolen base and was tagged out to end the inning with Junior Caminero at the plate pic.twitter.com/ukLb5ofLuW 
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 27, 2026 
 Such ends the Rays’ first inning.
 Brewers 0, Rays 0

 Link Copied!
 Junior Caminero makes his voice heard
 By Hannah Keyser 
 As the Rays watched their four-run lead slip away in Game 2, their 23-year-old slugger, Junior Caminero, was seen on the broadcast yelling emphatically in the dugout.
 Junior Caminero was fired up back in the Rays dugout after the Brewers tied up the game in the 6th pic.twitter.com/QmJljvYFMo 
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 25, 2026 
 ESPN wrote about how that moment was indicative of Caminero’s budding leadership on the club. He has become more vocal as the Rays have gone deeper into October, but it’s not an entirely new part of his personality.
 Kevin Ibach, the Rays assistant GM and vice president of player personnel, told CNN Sports a story about Caminero: Every year the organization brings some of their top American prospects down to the Dominican Republic, where Caminero is from originally, to help them understand and appreciate where many of their teammates learned the game.
 When they did so back in January this year, Caminero insisted on coming out to dinner to spend time with the young prospects.
 Junior Caminero is fired up for his introduction for @RaysBaseball ahead of Game 3 of the 2026 World Series pic.twitter.com/nQfh0p16qH 
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 26, 2026 
 “Junior’s sitting in the middle of that table, talking to them, asking them questions,” Ibach said. “In English, and that’s the most impressive thing.”
 Those are players who likely won’t debut in the majors for several seasons, teenagers now, although Caminero is not much older. It shows a level of commitment to the organization that the Rays are fortunate to have found in someone who is also capable of hitting a ball over 400 feet.

 Brewers threaten, but come up empty in the top of the first inning
 By Kevin Dotson 
 The dynamo that is the Brewers offense got off the a promising start in the first inning as Jackson Chourio ripped a single into center field.
 Leadoff single for Jackson Chourio and we're off in Tampa for Game 3 pic.twitter.com/F0imHsBSCv 
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 27, 2026 
 After Rays starter Freddy Peralta struck out Jake Bauers, Brewers captain Christian Yelich dropped a bloop single down the third base line and Peralta was in a jam three batters into the game.
 But Peralta successfully tiptoed through the minefield, inducing a popout from William Contreras followed by groundout from Brice Turang to end the inning.
 Score: Brewers 0, Rays 0 
 Read more 
 Link Copied!
 We are underway in Game 3
 By Kyle Feldscher 
 The aforementioned Freddy Peralta toes the rubber and fires the first pitch of Game 3 – a fastball that nearly hits Brewers leadoff hitter Jackson Chuorio.
 The entire series could hinge on the result of this game. Tampa needs to win to make sure it gets competitive in this series, whereas the Brewers would be on the verge of winning the championship with a victory.
 Nine tense innings await. Here we go!
 Read more 
 Link Copied!
 Freddy Peralta back in familiar form and squaring off against familiar faces
 By Hannah Keyser 
 Freddy Peralta pitches against the New York Yankees in the American League Division Series. 
 Mike Stobe/Getty Images 
 There are two distinct storylines to know about Freddy Peralta, the Rays’ ALCS MVP and Game 3 starter. The confluence of which makes it a little crazy that he’s pitching in the World Series – this year and against the Milwaukee Brewers.
 First, Peralta spent a decade in the Brewers’ organization. They acquired him as a minor leaguer and developed him into a multi-time All-Star. He’s been gone for less than a year, traded to the Mets this past January.
 “It is a little weird,” Peralta said before Game 2 about now facing his longtime club in the World Series.
 The reception from fans in Milwaukee was warm – they cheered him during introductions ahead of Game 1 and even shouted at him in the bullpen later that night: “We still love you!”
 “I was surprised to see it, but obviously very grateful. I didn’t know what to expect. Even some of my teammates here in Tampa Bay patted me on the back and said, ‘Hey, that was a great moment for you.’”
 Freddy Peralta, Brewers pitcher
 The second thing is that the trade to the Mets turned out to be a disaster. Coming off a season with a 2.70 ERA and the most wins in the National League, Peralta was a mess in New York, helping tank their World Series aspirations so thoroughly that they wound up as sellers at the deadline.
 What went wrong? “Sometimes I ask the same question myself,” Peralta said.
 He was dealt to the Rays in August, where they tinkered with his mechanics and reignited his confidence. Tampa fixed Freddy by treating him “ as a king ” and he has repaid them this October with an ERA just over 1 in four appearances. It’s a stunning turnaround.
 Peralta’s success with the Rays has drawn attention to their longtime pitching coach, Kyle Snyder. The 6-foot-8-inch former mediocre major leaguer is renowned for turning pitchers into the best versions of themselves – many of whom go on to cash in elsewhere. He does it with an embrace of cutting-edge technology and palpable concern for their personal well-being.
 “You get the environment right, you get the relationship right. Those things all matter,” Snyder told CNN Sports.
 Read more 
 Link Copied!
 Tropicana Field is World-Series-ready after being shuttered for the 2025 season
 By Kevin Dotson 
 The Brewers warm up at Tropicana Field before Game 3. 
 Mike Carlson/MLB Photos/Getty Images 
 The Rays are hosting their first World Series game since 2008, and their home stadium – the quirky Tropicana Field – is ready to meet the moment.
 This was no certainty heading into the 2026 season, after “The Trop” sustained significant damage from Hurricane Milton in October 2024. The domed stadium’s fabric roof was ripped to shreds by the powerful winds of the storm.
 The Rays spent the entire 2025 season playing their home games at cross-bay George M. Steinbrenner Field, the spring training home of the rival New York Yankees. And it was a race against the clock to get Tropicana Field ready for Opening Day this year.

 1:34

 Dramatic drone footage shows Tropicana Field roof blown off 
 1:34
 But here we are, six months later, and the Fall Classic has come to St. Petersburg, and Tropicana Field’s quirky architecture might be just what the Rays need to turn the momentum of this series. The roof of the Trop, which is nearly identical in color to a baseball and criss-crossed by a network of wires and catwalks – all of which are in play – has the potential to turn any game on its head.
 Depending on where a ball might strike the roof, it could result in an automatic home run or remain a live ball with the defensive players able to play the ball wherever it falls.
 For anyone new to Tampa Bay Rays baseball, buckle up and expect the unexpected.
 Tropicana Field is also known for its live stingrays that swim in a tank near the outfield.
